summary: G-CORE-3f mints the NEW 14th workspace crate `benten-drop` with a clean CBOR-on-disk DropBundle envelope, working envelope-sig + offline-consume pipeline, and 11/11 tf3f pins passing under both stable + MSRV-1.95 clippy. Crate-scaffolding + cross-language ErrorCode atomic-mirror (Rust 177→180 + TS 179→182 + ERROR-CATALOG.md) + most doc-coupling are correctly executed. Two findings warrant fix-now per HARD RULE 12: (1) MAJOR `docs/CRATES-DEEP-DIVE.md` + `docs/SCHEMA-DRIVEN-RENDERING.md` carry pre-existing 13-crate references that should bump to 14 in-wave (precedent: PR #1307 G-CORE-2 bumped CRATES-DEEP-DIVE 12→13 atomically with benten-crypto-suite landing — the discipline is in-wave); the agent dispositioned these as `out-of-wave per D-PHASE-3-10` which is INCORRECT for the live narrative docs (D-PHASE-3-10 covers passive `architecture_md_*` test files + historical backlog narrative, not the live deep-dive). (2) MINOR `EncryptedContent.bytes` opaque-blob couples Drop bundle wire-format to `encode_encrypted_node`'s explicitly-NOT-frozen storage-internal CBOR layout (G-CORE-3d docstring line 376) without naming this coupling in the bundle's on-disk-layout docstring; the design itself (opaque blob) is sound and is the right mitigation since G-CORE-9 can freeze both layers atomically, but the coupling must be visible. Three further MINOR observations on pim-18 SHAPE-not-SUBSTANCE substantiveness (per-Node-sig third-layer is a sized placeholder; defense-in-depth is really only 2 layers — envelope-sig + AEAD-tag — which is fine but the naming is inflated; agent does name G-CORE-9 freeze as the typed-Vec<Signature> upgrade point). No blockers; no architectural forks; merge-after-fix is the recommendation.

findings.title: EncryptedContent opaque-blob couples Drop wire-format to storage-internal encode_encrypted_node CBOR layout without naming the coupling in the on-disk-layout docstring
location: crates/benten-graph/src/aead_wrap.rs:375-376 — encode_encrypted_node docstring: `The format is internal to G-CORE-3d's storage layer and is NOT a frozen public surface (the v1 wire-freeze happens at G-CORE-9).`
findings.detail: The Drop bundle's `EncryptedContent.bytes` field stores the output of `benten_graph::aead_wrap::encode_encrypted_node` as opaque bytes. The opaque-blob design is SOUND — it avoids leaking storage-internal CBOR layout to the Drop public surface, and lets G-CORE-9 freeze both layers atomically. However, the Drop bundle's on-disk-layout docstring (lines 235-294) does NOT name this coupling: it describes `content: Vec<EncryptedContent>` as `the per-Recipe AEAD ciphertexts (each is a serialized EncryptedNode via encode_encrypted_node)` without flagging that the EncryptedNode encode format is explicitly NOT a frozen surface at HEAD. A future G-CORE-3d wave that mutates encode_encrypted_node's byte layout would silently break Drop bundle wire-format compatibility (P-III deployed-runtime hazard). The crate already names G-CORE-9 freeze for the per_node_attestation field (line 284) — adding a parallel callout for the content cells is symmetric.
findings.fix: Add a 2-3-line callout to the DropBundle on-disk-layout docstring (after line 249 `content: Vec<EncryptedContent>` entry) along the lines of: `Wire-format coupling: at G-CORE-3f, EncryptedContent.bytes wraps benten_graph::aead_wrap::encode_encrypted_node output, which is explicitly NOT a frozen public surface (storage-internal CBOR layout per G-CORE-3d). G-CORE-9 v1-interface freeze freezes BOTH layers atomically; any G-CORE-3d encode-format mutation pre-freeze MUST also retense this crate's DropBundle wire shape + the tf3f offline-consume pins.` This is a doc-only edit; no code change. Couples to a one-line cross-ref in crates/benten-graph/src/aead_wrap.rs line 376 (`see also crates/benten-drop/src/bundle.rs DropBundle docstring`) per §3.5g item #3.
findings.hard_rule_12_check: FIX-NOW is the correct disposition — the doc edit is trivial (~3 LOC) and makes a real P-III hazard visible to future maintainers.

findings.title: Per-Node-sig third defense-in-depth layer is a sized placeholder (vec![0xA5u8; 130]), not real per-Node Ed25519 signatures; defense-in-depth at G-CORE-3f is really 2 layers (envelope-sig + AEAD-tag)
location: crates/benten-drop/src/bundle.rs:705-723 — build_5_recipe_bundle_impl synthesizes per_node_attestation as `vec![0xA5u8; content.len() * 26]`
crates/benten-drop/src/bundle.rs:156-164 — DropBundleError::PerNodeSignatureInvalid variant DEFINED but never constructed in production paths

crates/benten-drop/tests/tf3f_envelope_plus_per_node_sig_defense_in_depth.rs:131-162 — PIN 3 measures bundle-size delta only; does not exercise per-Node-sig verification (because no such verification exists at G-CORE-3f)
findings.detail: The crate-level docs (lib.rs:30-47) describe `Two cryptographic layers protect bundle integrity: envelope-sig (outer) + per-Node AEAD authentication tags (inner)` — this is accurate (2 layers). However, the per_node_attestation field, the PerNodeSignatureInvalid error variant, the `per-Node-sig defense-in-depth` wave name, and the PIN 3 test name (`tf3f_defense_in_depth_overhead_under_12_percent` / `envelope_plus_per_node_sig_defense_in_depth.rs`) collectively imply a THIRD per-Node-sig layer that doesn't actually verify anything at G-CORE-3f — `per_node_attestation` is a sized byte placeholder (`vec![0xA5u8; 130]`) used solely for the bundle-size overhead measurement. PIN 3 measures (size_with - size_without) / size_without < 12% — true, but `size_with` is inflated by 130 bytes of pattern bytes, not real Ed25519-sig bytes. This is honest in the field docstring (line 284-285 names G-CORE-9 as the typed-Vec<Signature> upgrade point) but the wave-name + test-name + error-variant-existence-without-construction collectively inflate the apparent defense-in-depth surface. PIN 1 (per_node_ciphertext_tamper_detected_envelope_sig_still_valid) IS substantive — it exercises the AEAD-tag defense (real) — so the load-bearing 2-layer defense is actually pinned. The MINOR is that the framing oversells the cryptographic surface; future operators reading the bundle docs might believe per-Node-sigs verify when they don't.
findings.fix: (a) Update the PIN 3 test name + docstring to say `tf3f_per_node_attestation_size_overhead_under_12_percent` (or similar) + the body comment to clarify it measures the sized placeholder's overhead as the surface reservation for the typed-Vec<Signature> upgrade at G-CORE-9. (b) In bundle.rs line 717-722 (the per_node_attestation construction), add a `// G-CORE-3f: this is a SIZED PLACEHOLDER, not real per-Node Ed25519 signatures. The placeholder reserves the wire-shape budget; G-CORE-9 freeze upgrades it to typed Vec<Signature> parallel to content.` Per pim-18, this preserves the SUBSTANTIVE 2-layer pin (envelope-sig + AEAD-tag) while honestly naming the reserved-but-not-yet-built third layer. ~5 LOC. Alternatively if the dispatching orchestrator believes the reservation is over-engineered for G-CORE-3f, the per_node_attestation field could be deferred entirely until G-CORE-9 with a §4.x phase-4-meta-backlog row carrying the reservation — but the size-reservation argument is reasonable for forward-compat.
findings.hard_rule_12_check: FIX-NOW per the 3-LOC-honesty-comment shape; nothing structurally wrong, just naming inflation that creates a documentation-vs-reality gap.

findings.title: tf3f_inline_tiny_synthetic_bundle_rejected_typed actually exercises UnsupportedDropVersion path, not UnsupportedDropMode
location: crates/benten-drop/src/bundle.rs:585-599 — synthesize_inline_tiny_cbor_for_test emits Synthetic(0xFFFE) version, not a Mode-3-shaped bundle
crates/benten-drop/src/bundle.rs:325-339 — parse_cbor_bytes only checks version; never reaches Mode-3 reject path (because no InlineTiny enum arm exists)
findings.detail: The agent self-reports this honestly: `fixture synthesize_inline_tiny_cbor_for_test emits Synthetic(0xFFFE) version → parser returns UnsupportedDropVersion`. The structural pin (PIN 1, the exhaustive non-wildcard match against DropContentMode arms) IS the substantive defer-to-post-v1 defense — and that's correct: the absence of an InlineTiny enum arm means the parser can NEVER see a Mode-3 bundle over the wire (CBOR deserialization fails before reaching the parser's mode-check), so there's no runtime path that could surface UnsupportedDropMode for a Mode-3 attempt. The MINOR is that the PIN 2 test name (`tf3f_inline_tiny_synthetic_bundle_rejected_typed`) + the existence of `DropBundleError::UnsupportedDropMode` + `E_DROP_BUNDLE_MODE3_INLINE_REJECTED` suggest a runtime rejection path that's actually unreachable. The test accepts EITHER UnsupportedDropMode OR UnsupportedDropVersion — meaning the test would PASS if a future commit removed the UnsupportedDropMode variant entirely, because the version path covers it. This is a real pim-18 concern: the SHAPE (typed-error-variant + ErrorCode) is wired but the SUBSTANCE (actual reachable code path for Mode-3 reject) is structurally absent.
findings.fix: Two reasonable shapes (orchestrator picks): (a) Update the PIN 2 test name + docstring to clarify it asserts the defer-to-post-v1 contract via version-discriminator hijack (`tf3f_inline_tiny_path_defer_to_post_v1_via_version_or_mode_rejection`), explaining the structural absence makes UnsupportedDropMode currently unreachable. OR (b) wire a real Mode-3 reject path: add a `mode_raw_u8` byte to the parser that fails BEFORE serde_cbor's enum-deserialization succeeds; this way the UnsupportedDropMode arm is actually reachable. (a) is the cheaper honest path; (b) is more defense-in-depth but adds complexity for a deferred-to-post-v1 surface. Recommend (a) — ~5-LOC test-rename + comment. The E_DROP_BUNDLE_MODE3_INLINE_REJECTED ErrorCode can stay reserved for the future Mode-3 wave's typed reject without code change.
findings.hard_rule_12_check: FIX-NOW (option a) per the 5-LOC bound; the defense-in-depth-via-structural-absence is real, just needs honest naming.
